scope: Harmonic creativity, not measured perceived emotion

methodology.reviewed: Official publisher abstracts and open-access scholarly articles; no claim of reading paywalled full books
methodology.limitation: No melody, rhythm, tempo, timbre, register, dynamic, phrase or listener ratings captured by web harmonic input

evidenceLevels.A: Full open-access academic article/primary abstract and verified bibliographic record
evidenceLevels.B: Publisher book description or chapter abstract only

methodology.revision: Five fuzzy creative neighborhoods in UI; explicitly separate listener affect constructs from compositional intents. Valence/arousal research informs the simplification, but no quantitative emotion coordinates are inferred from bare chords.

sources.title: Emotions Evoked by the Sound of Music: Characterization, Classification, and Measurement
sources.claim: Four studies developed and supported the nine-factor GEMS instrument; GEMS measures music-induced emotional states, not harmony-only effects.

sources.title: Emotion-to-Music Mapping Atlas (EMMA)
sources.claim: GEMS dimensions and higher-order sublimity/vitality/unease; real listening ratings required.

sources.title: Emotional responses to music: the need to consider underlying mechanisms
sources.claim: Musical expectancy is only one of several mechanisms of induced emotion.

sources.title: Emotion and Meaning in Music
sources.claim: Pattern, expectation and completion are prominent topics, not a ready-made emotion/chord mapping.

sources.title: Sweet Anticipation: Music and the Psychology of Expectation
sources.claim: Five expectation response systems and their possible role in music.

sources.title: Tonal Pitch Space
sources.claim: Pitch-space distance, tonal tension and attraction models; not directly listener emotion.

sources.title: Modeling Tonal Tension
sources.claim: Prolongation, pitch space, surface tension and attraction tested against listeners' tension reports.

sources.title: Perception of musical tension in short chord sequences
sources.claim: Tension judgments combine tonal, sensory and horizontal movement effects and differ by training.

sources.title: Moderating effects of chord progressions on the emotional experience of major and minor chords
sources.claim: Major/minor differences in pleasantness, stability and tension depend on stability of progression endings.

sources.title: Bodily maps of uncertainty and surprise in musical chord progression
sources.claim: Chord-sequence uncertainty and prediction error relate to emotional response and bodily sensations; not individual deterministic prediction.

sources.title: Hollywood Harmony: Chapter 5 Pantriadic Wonder
sources.claim: In some film music, pantriadic chromaticism and wonder/awe/frisson have a theorized relationship; not universal.

sources.title: Hollywood Cadences: Music and the Structure of Cinematic Expectation
sources.claim: Phrase-level cadential genres can shape narrative expectations; no cadence proven from lone chord.

sources.title: The Relationship between Musical Structure and Perceived Expression
sources.claim: Perceived expression depends on multiple interacting structural factors; typical musical variables show less clear effects than raw auditory cues.

sources.title: A Quantitative, Parametric Model of Musical Tension
sources.claim: Tension modeled with harmony, register, melody, dynamics, event density, tempo and rhythmic regularity.

sources.title: The major-minor mode dichotomy in music perception
sources.claim: Major/minor expression is culturally, experientially and contextually modulated.

sources.title: A comparison of the discrete and dimensional models of emotion in music
sources.claim: In 116 non-musician listeners assessing film-music excerpts, categorical and dimensional reports broadly corresponded, but discrete categories had poorer resolution for ambiguous examples.

sources.title: Measuring music-induced emotion: A comparison of emotion models, personality biases, and intensity of experiences
sources.claim: In 148 participants listening to 16 film cues, dimensional valence/arousal models gave high consistency; personality and mood influenced reports.

sources.title: What emotions does music express? Structure of affect terms in music using iterative crowdsourcing paradigm
sources.claim: Study of music-expressed affect found valid 7- and compact 4-factor structures; music-expressed categories differed from those of music-induced emotion. No unique fixed number of musical emotions.

sources.title: What does music express? Basic emotions and beyond
sources.claim: Emotion conveyed by music has multiple layers and may vary with context, associations and listener; distinguish conveyed from personally felt emotion.

gems.warning: No validated mapping to harmonic symbols or fifteen Cinemático intents.

creativeDesign.mappingStatus: C: internal exploratory design hypotheses, not experimental GEMS classification
creativeDesign.ranking: Context continuity plus modest gesture-bias, no fitted statistical parameters or trained model

neighborhoods.scope: Five flexible creative neighborhoods chosen for Cinemático usability, NOT validated listener clusters or a GEMS factor model.
neighborhoods.operationalPrinciple: Preserve existing individual creative intent if selected; the group is navigation and soft context, not a forced emotional judgment.

negativeControls.rule: Do not infer a confirmed A minor key or a specific felt emotion from isolated Am.
Ambiguous key; D major added later is a mode-color change, not automatically uplift.
Functional cadence hypothesis supports a tonal arrival but not necessarily joy.
Suspended Csus4 ending is not a resolved C chord despite root identity.
Same relative pitch-class material may be heard differently according to tonality/phrase/tempo.
Maj7 does not imply nostalgia or tenderness without additional structure and listening.
